title: Opportunity matrix: GPU waste by pool (weekly export)
body:
Purpose:
This is a dashboard export intended for quick ops prioritization: identify which GPU pools and clusters are contributing the most 'waste' (idle time, fragmentation, preempt/reschedule churn) over the last 7 days and surface high-leverage remediation ideas. Not a canonical final report — working notes + numbers from the dashboard CSV + eyeball-driven recommendations.

Scope / notes on methodology:
- Window: 2026-09-06T00:00 to 2026-09-12T23:59 (UTC). Weekly boundary aligned to Monday UTC to match capacity cycles.
- Sources: live dashboard export (per-cluster/per-pool CSV), scheduler logs (preempt/reschedule events), spot/preemptible metrics, and allocation table snapshot at 00:00 each day.
- Definitions used in this sheet:
  - idle_minutes: aggregate minutes where GPU utilization (GPU% avg) < 8% while instance was allocated to a non-empty job.
  - fragmentation_score: heuristic score (0-1) indicating wasted GPU slots due to container packing inefficiencies; higher is worse.
  - churn_cost_est: estimated token of cost from job preemption/reschedule (minutes * cost_rate).
  - reclaimable_minutes: subset of idle_minutes we believe can be recaptured via autoscaler tuning / packing / backfill (~ conservative estimate).
- Confidence: medium — allocation and job-level telemetry has 5-10% sampling gaps; numbers below are rounded to nearest 10 minutes / $10.

Top-level weekly numbers (fleet-level aggregated):
- total_allocated_gpu_hours: 124,520 GPU-hours
- estimated_idle_gpu_hours: 4,380 GPU-hours (~3.5% of allocated)
- estimated_reclaimable_hours: 2,050 GPU-hours (~46% of idle)
- estimated_weekly_waste_cost: $38,200 (based on blended cost rate)
- major drivers: small interactive jobs stuck on large instances, short-lived retries after preemption, and several pools with high reserved-but-unused headroom.

Per-region highlights (ranked by reclaimable hours):
- NA (North America): reclaimable_hours 980, main sources: dev-sandbox-pools, dedicated-canary-pools. Notes: dev-sandbox had many long-running low-utilization debug sessions.
- EU (Europe): reclaimable_hours 610, main sources: batch-starvation in eu-batch-2 and 4, plus mis-sized mlflow experiments pinned to 8-GPU nodes.
- APAC: reclaimable_hours 460, main sources: burst pools with conservative autoscaler thresholds and high preemption churn.

Opportunity matrix (top 8 pool-level rows from export):
Columns: pool | cluster | pool_type | avg_gpu_util_pct | idle_hours | fragmentation_score | reclaimable_hours | immediate_action | expected_recovery_hours 
1) dev-sandbox-small | cluster-a1 | sandbox | 12% | 420h | 0.42 | 300h | reduce max node size to 1xA100; enable shared-small packing | 240h
2) dedicated-canary | cluster-b3 | dedicated | 8% | 360h | 0.28 | 220h | change autoscaler scale-down aggressive; short TTL on pre-boot reserved nodes | 180h
3) eu-batch-2 | cluster-e2 | batch | 18% | 240h | 0.33 | 140h | allow smaller job bin packing and increase preemption window from 30s -> 90s | 120h
4) apac-burst | cluster-c7 | burst | 9% | 200h | 0.45 | 160h | adjust burst threshold and increase backfill aggressiveness | 130h
5) experiments-8x | cluster-d5 | experiments | 14% | 160h | 0.55 | 120h | introduce 4-GPU flavor; default experiments template to use smaller nodes | 100h
6) reserve-high-headroom | cluster-a2 | reserved | 22% | 120h | 0.20 | 60h | re-evaluate reservation sizing vs committed throughput | 50h
7) training-large | cluster-f1 | training | 35% | 80h | 0.15 | 40h | recommend QOS lower priority for small jobs in this pool | 30h
8) shared-inference | cluster-g4 | inference | 72% | 0h | 0.02 | 0h | none | 0h

Quick charts/text slices included in export (verbatim lines from CSV):
- "cluster, pool, day, avg_gpu_util, allocated_hours, idle_hours, preemptions, fragmentation_score"
- example row: "cluster-a1,dev-sandbox-small,2026-09-08,10.4,120,70,4,0.46"

Operational notes & hypotheses:
- Dev sandbox pools are the single biggest near-term win. A combination of default node flavor (8-GPU) and interactive notebooks left running are creating large isolated idle blocks. A small-ticket change to offer 1x/2x flavors (and nudges in the UI) could reclaim ~60% of that.
- Preemption/retry churn is concentrated on apac-burst due to very short preemption windows and high spot volatility. Increasing the preemption grace/window and using graceful checkpoints for long jobs reduces churn cost.
- Fragmentation_score correlates strongly with the proportion of small jobs running on large nodes; we should add an alert when fragmentation_score > 0.4 for >6 hours.

Short action list (owner / ETA / impact):
- Aisha: implement alert for fragmentation_score > 0.4 (infra-metrics, 2d) — impact: catch rising waste earlier
- Connor: rollout 1x/2x node flavors in dev-sandbox templates (infra + dx, 5d) — impact: reclaim ~240h/week
- Miguel: adjust burst pool autoscaler window and backfill policy for apac-burst (3d) — impact: reduce churn cost by estimated $6k/week
- Elena: run a 72-hour experiment with aggressive scale-down on dedicated-canary (ops-runbook, 7d) — impact: validate 60-80% of expected reclaimable hours

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How many of the idle_minutes are due to long-running training logs / tensorboard sessions? (Need job-level sampling: INFRA-7124)
- Could we auto-suspend idle notebook sessions after 12h inactivity? UX/Policy discussion needed.
- Is there an economic threshold where adding a 4-GPU flavor increases scheduling overhead more than the reclaimed cost? Run simulation in perf-lab.

Appendix: quick checksum of raw top-of-export numbers pulled from CSV (rounded):
- rows processed: 18,142
- clusters: 52
- distinct pools: 28
- missing telemetry rows: ~1.8%

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working export; if numbers look surprising, check the raw CSV attached in the linked artifacts (PR #987) and the job-sampler logs. We should convert promising rows above into tracked tickets (INFRA-7124 flagged).
- Prefer shipping low-risk quick wins first (node flavors + fragmentation alert) and run the canary scale-down experiment before broad policy changes.
